description_full: Dell Technologies Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, markets, sells, and supports various comprehensive and integrated solutions, products, and services in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and internationally. The company operates through Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) and Client Solutions Group (CSG) segments. The ISG segment provides modern and traditional storage solutions, including all-flash, purpose-built, hyper-converged infrastructure, software-defined storage, and general-purpose and AI-optimized servers. This segment also offers networking products and services comprising wide area network infrastructure, data center and edge networking switches, and cables and optics that help its business customers to transform and modernize their infrastructure and complementing its server and storage solutions; and software, peripherals, and services, including consulting and support, and deployment. The CSG segment provides notebooks, desktops, and workstations and branded peripherals that include displays, docking stations, keyboards, mice, webcam and audio devices, and third-party software and peripherals; and configuration, and extended warranties services. The company is involved in originating, collecting, and servicing customer financing arrangements and offers payment and consumption solutions and services, such utility, subscription, as-a-service, leases, and loans, as well as fixed-term leases and loans. It serves enterprises, governmental agencies and other public institutions, educational institutions, healthcare organizations, small and medium-sized businesses, and consumers. The company has a strategic alliance with Rafay Systems for the development of AI infrastructure solutions. The company was formerly known as Denali Holding Inc. and changed its name to Dell Technologies Inc. in March 2013. Dell Technologies Inc. was founded in 1984 and is headquartered in Round Rock, Texas.

financial_summary: Dell Technologies Inc. is a mega-cap technology business with a $208.9B market cap on $113.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 26% against a 11% cost of capital — a 15-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 22% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $8.6B in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.88× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.2×.

Shareholder yield of 3.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 7.7% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 7% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.31x its revenue share).
It accounts for 2.6% of sector revenue and 0.8% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-8.5% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 288% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 27% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 45% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 80% and a beta of 1.39, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 2.76 vs 5y 1.73), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $3.1B traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 46% in the 2020 crash and 44% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $306 (margin of safety -7%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 39%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $165 to $559 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 19.1 vs 26.7 and EV/EBITDA 12.7 vs 16.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 208% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.1% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 25 covering analysts target $590 on average, 80% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 26% clears the cost of capital of 10.7% by 15pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.98).
It runs a 22% gross margin and converts 8% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.88x.
It spends 2.8% of revenue on R&D and 0.6% on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.8x net debt to EBITDA ($11.5B of cash against $31.5B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 5.2x.
The current ratio of 0.91 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
It runs on negative working capital (-37 days), so customers and suppliers effectively fund its operations.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 3.5% over 3 years and 3.8% over 5 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 64% of profits supports about 16.4% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -1.7% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.39 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 72% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 4%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.9x, 2.3% of sales), a maintenance pace.
own: Insiders own 7.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 77%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (86 sales, net $89.0M sold).
It returns 3.6% a year to shareholders (2.9% in buybacks and 0.8% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 3.6% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 97,000 employees, each generates about $1.2M of revenue, 3.1x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 7.0% a year.
That works out to $88K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $3.4M (3x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (10/10, lower is better).
